title: Progressive Lightsaber Training — Dynamic Defense Drills
summary: A supervised ten-minute defensive training session with randomized bounded attacks, four progressive cadence levels, recovery intervals, and an automatic guard return after every exchange.

cues.text: TRAINING CHECK: clear the full arm and prop envelope; use the approved lightweight breakaway prop and protective equipment; verify arm calibration and communications; keep the base stationary; place a second operator at the physical E-stop; then arm supervised saber choreography. Stop immediately for tracking error, unexpected sound, contact, stale feedback, or a person entering the exclusion zone.

Welcome to progressive saber defense training. Each exchange is selected dynamically from a bounded family of directions, so memorize the principles rather than a fixed sequence. The first level emphasizes recognition. Later levels shorten the requested movement time and add combinations while preserving the same workspace and actuator-side validation. Return to a stable guard after every defense.
Intermediate level begins. Watch the initial direction without guessing, move only after recognition, and recover your stance before the next exchange. The trainer now varies height as well as side.

Advanced level begins. Exchanges may contain three linked directions. Maintain balance, avoid overcommitting to the first motion, and use the recovery interval. Difficulty comes from combination and timing, not an expanded robot workspace.

EXPERT LEVEL CHECK: continue only if every prior exchange tracked normally, the prop remains secure, the area remains clear, the participant requests progression, and the E-stop operator is ready. Otherwise stop here or repeat an earlier level.

Expert level begins with longer combinations and the shortest validated host-side duration in this training profile. It does not bypass Amber firmware limits. Prioritize clean defense and distance; stop rather than chasing a missed exchange.

Training complete. Record which directions caused late recognition, whether the robot reached each requested pose, and whether measured motion matched the requested duration. Progress by consistency rather than by skipping levels. Disarm choreography before anyone enters the robot workspace.
Disarm saber choreography, deactivate the arm using the verified shutdown procedure, and confirm the prop has stopped before entering the workspace.
